CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Katingan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Katingan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Katingan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Katingan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public and or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Violence against women is any action or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, mentally sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or private life.
11. Victims of violence against women and children are individuals or groups, who experience misery and or suffering as a result of violence and or threats of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will, is or has occurred.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution/organization/agency providing services to victims of violence against women and children who is trained or has expertise in accordance with their competence and authority in providing assistance to victims of violence in accordance with the type of service provided.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family members, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions and/or legal apparatus which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence in accordance with their competence and authority.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a functional technical implementation unit as the organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination and other problems.
20. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
21. Minimum Service Standards abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for UPTD PPA services in providing complaint handling services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
22. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 3
Protection of Women and Children victims of violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of violence against women and children;
b. protect women and children as well as provide services to women and Children victims of violence; and
c. empower women and Children victims of violence.

Article 8
(1) The community may participate and be responsible in services, prevention, assistance, recovery and monitoring of victims of violence.
(2) Community participation and responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

Article 9
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear.
Paragraph (2) Letter a Sufficiently Clear.
Letter b What is meant by "health rehabilitation" is action provided to restore the physical, psychological, and social functions of victims as a result of the violence they experienced in order to restore bodily functions that are experiencing problems.
Letter c What is meant by "social rehabilitation" is the process of restoring functions and development that enables victims to carry out their social functions properly in community life.
Letter d What is meant by "legal aid" is the guarantee of legal protection and guarantee of equality before the law for victims.
Letter e Sufficiently Clear.
Letter f Sufficiently Clear.
Letter g What is meant by "repatriation" is the effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin.
What is meant by "social reintegration" is the development effort carried out to provide opportunities for the community and victims of violence to interact and socialize with each other to eliminate existing negative stigma.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently Clear.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

Article 6
Child victims of violence, in addition to obtaining the rights as referred to in Article 5, also obtain special rights as follows:
a. respect for survival, growth and development;
b. to education, health and access to parents during the handling process; and
c. to obtain equal protection related to status, citizenship, race, skin color, gender, language, religion, politics, disability, birth or other status.
- 6 -

Article 14
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear.
Paragraph (2) Point a Sufficiently Clear.
Point b Sufficiently Clear.
Point c Sufficiently Clear.
Point d Sufficiently Clear.
Point e What is meant by Monitoring is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies and activities for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
Point f What is meant by Evaluation is an activity of collecting information regarding the performance of something, where such information will be used to determine the best alternative in making decisions.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently Clear.

CHAPTER XI
FUNDING
Article 16
* \ Funds for the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence, are sourced from:
a. APBN
b. APBD; and
c. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.
Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to achieve welfare.
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by "local wisdom" is good cultural values that exist within the Katingan community.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to life, survival and development of children" is a moral principle that every person has the right to live, maintain their life and livelihood, as well as improve their standard of living.
Letter g What is meant by "respect for victims' opinions" is the government recognizes and ensures that victims can express their opinions and are given the opportunity to express their views freely on all matters that affect them.
Letter h What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.

CHAPTER VII
SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSE
Article 12
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or Safe House.
(2) The Social Protection House and/or Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) is to guarantee the implementation of services by the UPTD PPA.
(3) For the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may utilize social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to achieve welfare.
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.

Letter g What is meant by "respect for victims' opinions" is the government recognizes and ensures that victims can express their opinions and are given the opportunity to express their views freely on all matters that affect them.
Letter h What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.

12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

15. REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Katingan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Katingan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Katingan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Katingan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public and or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Violence against women is any action or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, mentally sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or private life.
11. Victims of violence against women and children are individuals or groups, who experience misery and or suffering as a result of violence and or threats of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will, is or has occurred.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution/organization/agency providing services to victims of violence against women and children who is trained or has expertise in accordance with their competence and authority in providing assistance to victims of violence in accordance with the type of service provided.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family members, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions and/or legal apparatus which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence in accordance with their competence and authority.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a functional technical implementation unit as the organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination and other problems.
20. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
21. Minimum Service Standards abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for UPTD PPA services in providing complaint handling services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
22. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Letter g What is meant by "respect for victims' opinions" is the government recognizes and ensures that victims can express their opinions and are given the opportunity to express their views freely on all matters that affect them.
Letter h What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.

REGARDING

I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.

15. REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.
Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to achieve welfare.
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by "local wisdom" is good cultural values that exist within the Katingan community.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to life, survival and development of children" is a moral principle that every person has the right to live, maintain their life and livelihood, as well as improve their standard of living.
Letter g What is meant by "respect for victims' opinions" is the government recognizes and ensures that victims can express their opinions and are given the opportunity to express their views freely on all matters that affect them.
Letter h What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Katingan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Katingan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Katingan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Katingan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public and or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Violence against women is any action or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, mentally sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or private life.
11. Victims of violence against women and children are individuals or groups, who experience misery and or suffering as a result of violence and or threats of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will, is or has occurred.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution/organization/agency providing services to victims of violence against women and children who is trained or has expertise in accordance with their competence and authority in providing assistance to victims of violence in accordance with the type of service provided.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family members, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions and/or legal apparatus which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence in accordance with their competence and authority.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a functional technical implementation unit as the organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination and other problems.
20. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
21. Minimum Service Standards abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for UPTD PPA services in providing complaint handling services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
22. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 3
Protection of Women and Children victims of violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of violence against women and children;
b. protect women and children as well as provide services to women and Children victims of violence; and
c. empower women and Children victims of violence.

Article 8
(1) The community may participate and be responsible in services, prevention, assistance, recovery and monitoring of victims of violence.
(2) Community participation and responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities;
c. providing emergency assistance; and
d. providing protection to victims of violence.

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear.

Letter d What is meant by "legal aid" is the guarantee of legal protection and guarantee of equality before the law for victims.
Letter e Sufficiently Clear.
Letter f Sufficiently Clear.
Letter g What is meant by "repatriation" is the effort to return victims of violence to their area of origin.
What is meant by "social reintegration" is the development effort carried out to provide opportunities for the community and victims of violence to interact and socialize with each other to eliminate existing negative stigma.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently Clear.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, then the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by "local wisdom" is good cultural values that exist within the Katingan community.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to life, survival and development of children" is a moral principle that every person has the right to live, maintain their life and livelihood, as well as improve their standard of living.

Letter h What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

REGARDING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's aspirations, so that every child has the right to survival, to grow and develop, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women and families, society and the state will produce resilient generations who will continue the nation's aspirations.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Katingan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children victims of violence so that it needs to be regulated in Regional Regulations.
So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the regions so that institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, administration, handling, empowerment, guidance and supervision of the protection of women and children in Katingan Regency.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Katingan Regency.

6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.

9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.

15. 17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family members, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

20. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
21. Minimum Service Standards abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for UPTD PPA services in providing complaint handling services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
22. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Letter h What is meant by "legal certainty" is the existence of legal norms that do not conflict with other regulations and provide legal security for victims of violence from the arbitrariness of certain parties.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Katingan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Katingan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Katingan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Katingan Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public and or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Violence against women is any action or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, mentally sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or private life.
11. Victims of violence against women and children are individuals or groups, who experience misery and or suffering as a result of violence and or threats of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will, is or has occurred.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution/organization/agency providing services to victims of violence against women and children who is trained or has expertise in accordance with their competence and authority in providing assistance to victims of violence in accordance with the type of service provided.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family members, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions and/or legal apparatus which includes providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence in accordance with their competence and authority.
19. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a functional technical implementation unit as the organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination and other problems.
20. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from handling complaints, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
21. Minimum Service Standards abbreviated as SPM are performance benchmarks for UPTD PPA services in providing complaint handling services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal aid, recovery/psychological services, mediation up to repatriation and social reintegration.
22. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
